articleTitle: Research on omnidirectional ORB-SLAM2 for mobile robots
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper proposes a method of using omnidirectional images as visual input to ORB-SLAM2 system. With it, the system can track ORB feature points in the whole 360°. Hence, compared to traditional monocular camera SLAM systems, the result will be much more robust since more ORB feature points can be extracted. To implement this scheme, the main task lies in processing the distorted omnidirectional image. In this paper, we describe an algorithm of turning the omnidirectional images into correct inputs to the ORB-SLAM2. It includes ORB feature extraction algorithm on sphere surface, area selection and image transformation. Additionally, to reduce the algorithm's time cost, we also add some new methods like pre-rotation estimation and optimization in feature points matching.

articleTitle: A Review of Rotary Modulation Technology Applied to Strapdown Inertial Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Rotary modulation technology is a skill that can improve the accuracy of inertial navigation system by self-compensating without any external message. This method can eliminate slowly varying error by staying equal time in the opposite position of a circumference. Nowadays, rotary modulation technology has been applied to many kinds of inertial navigation systems, such as MK49 and wsn-7a in America and Omega system in Russia and so on. According to the current situation, improving gyroscopes' accuracy would be really difficult. Therefore, rotary modulation technology is an important direction for inertial navigation system. This article summarizes the development history of rotary modulation strapdown inertial navigation system, analyses and concludes 4 key technologies of the system: Gyroscope technology, Rotating mechanism technology, Strapdown algorithm technology and Self-calibration technology. According to the time order, gyroscopes can be categorized into 5 kinds: mechanical gyro, laser gyro, fiber optic gyro, MEMS gyro and atomic gyro. With the development of inertia technology, the performance of the gyro has improved gradually, the mechanical structure becomes simpler, and the cost and the volume decline sharply. However, the drift error still exists and is always a main kind error of gyros. The rotary modulation technology is specially aimed at eliminating drift error to improve inertial navigation systems' accuracy. Rotating mechanism has several key parts: the number of axis that be modulated, the way of rotation and the angle between gyro's axis and rotation axis. If single-axis modulation is adopted, the drift error can be only eliminated in 2 directions. So, 2 and 3 axis rotary modulation methods have been developed to eliminate more drift errors. As for rotating mode, there are continuous rotating, positive-negative rotating and operative-halted rotating. In order to realize modulating all drift errors in 3 axis, offset-axis rotary modulation method has been developed. While doing navigation calculating, the rotation of inertia components must be considered. Traditional calibration methods use Kalman Filter but the observability is not so good when in the static base condition, which will slow down the rate of convergence and decline the filtering precision. After using rotary modulation technology, the rotation of the inertia components will improve the observability of the system, which will finally improve precision. As for alignment, rotary modulation technology can also improve its precision because rotating mechanism can provide a continuous moving base to increase the observability. In the end, this article discusses the advantages and disadvantages of rotary modulation SINS and the future direction of this technology.

articleTitle: A rotation scheme for dual-unit inertial navigation system based on MEMS sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Inertial navigation system (INS) based on Micro-Electro-Mechanical System (MEMS) has been used in the both civil and military fields. However, large errors such as bias errors restrict them from being applied widely. Rotating modulation technique is a mature method which can modulate the constant errors of MEMS. In this way, all the devices' errors can be modulated if INS has two axes. Dual-axis INS has different forms of organizational structures which will affect the error propagation characteristics. Traditional dual-axis RINS cannot modulate all the devices' errors at the same time, in this paper, dual-unit RINS is studied and an improved rotation scheme is proposed. Theoretical analysis proves that the performance of the reported scheme is better than the traditional dual-axis RINS. Simulation results based on Matlab show that the performance of the dual-unit RINS with proposed rotation scheme is much better than the traditional dual-axis RINS with an eight-position scheme, whose position accuracy is better than the strap-down mode. What is more, the dual-unit RINS can improve the fault-tolerant performance of the system.

articleTitle: Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control Based on UKF Identification
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: To improve the estimation result of the linear extended state observer (LESO), we propose a linear active disturbance rejection control strategy based on the UKF identification. We use the UKF identification method to identify the unknown parameters of the system model and the controller gain b<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> of the linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC), thereby reducing the uncertain factors of the controlled system and improving the ability of the LESO to estimate the generalized disturbance of the system. The proposed control strategy is applied to the rotor-driving system. The simulation results show that the proposed method has better control effect compared with the traditional LADRC, and the estimation ability of the linear extended state observer is stronger.

articleTitle: Multi UAVs Cooperative Reconnaissance Path Planning in Obstacles Environment (IEEE/CSAA GNCC)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Multiple UAVs cooperative reconnaissance path planning in complex polygonal obstacles environment is presented in this paper. Firstly, different reconnaissance mission models are formulated, such as sensor sensing, effective reconnaissance duration time and so on. Secondly, considering different mission constraints and requirements, a two-step multiple UAVs cooperative reconnaissance path planning framework based on Dubins curve is established. Besides, a heuristic obstacle-free path planning in the presence of polygonal obstacles is designed, which is satisfied with UAV kinematic constraint. The simulation result demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Dense Mapping from Feature-Based Monocular SLAM Based on Depth Prediction
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In recent years some direct monocular SLAM methods have appeared achieving impressive semi-dense or dense 3D scene reconstruction. At the same time, feature-based monocular SLAM methods can obtain more accurate trajectory than direct methods, but only obtain sparse feature point map rather than semi-dense or even dense map like direct methods. With the development of deep learning, it becomes possible to predict the depth map of a scene given a single RGB image. In this paper we demonstrate how depth prediction module via deep learning can be used as a plug-in module in highly accurate feature-based monocular SLAM (e.g. ORB-SLAM). Both accurate trajectory from ORB-SLAM and dense 3D reconstruction from depth prediction can be achieved. Evaluation results show that dense scene reconstruction can be obtained from highly accurate feature-based monocular SLAM.

articleTitle: Target Identification Technique Based on Track Filtering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This study investigated an improve anti-jamming techniques based on Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) for radar seekers during the terminal guidance stage, a target identification technique for the typical range-velocity joint drawing-out (RVJDO) deception jamming model is presented. First, an RVJDO jamming model was built. On this basis, by introducing the relative missile-target range, radial velocity, elevation angle and azimuth, a system tracking model was subsequently built. Second, a UKF framework for target tracking and identification as well as UKF-based target identification metrics was provided. Finally, a simulation experiment was performed based on a typical target motion (circling) model. In this experiment, a target that launched four RVJDO jamming attacks was identified. The simulation results showed that the UKF information could help achieve effective target identification under RVJDO jamming attacks. In addition, the simulation results also validated the feasibility and effectiveness of the identification method developed in this study.

articleTitle: A Self-organized Reciprocal Control Method for Multi-Agent Coverage
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Multi-agent coverage problem is an active issue of how to cover an accessible region of interest by agents. In this paper, a self-organized reciprocal control method is proposed, which is directly optimized in velocity space, different from the traditional method modeled in configuration space. The method considers the reciprocal of neighboring agents that is ignored by most other methods. And the motion of each agent is collision-free motivated by this method. The simulation results corroborate that the proposed method has higher coverage rate, faster convergence rate and less deadweight loss than other traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Cooperative Approach to Multi-UAVs Search for Mobile Targets Based on Pigeon-Inspired Optimization
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: To improve the search efficiency and reduce the impact of the uncertainty of mobile targets on multi-UAVs search, this paper proposes a search decision-making method based on the receding horizon control (RHC) and pigeon-inspired optimization (PIO). According to advance intelligence information and detection information of onboard sensors, the search environment is described with the target occupancy probability updated based on the Bayesian theory. In order to describe the search environment more accurately, we also introduce certainty information and pheromone information. Then under the conditions of targets discovery profit, expected detection profit, cooperation profit and the execution cost, the cooperative profit function is built. Aiming at reducing the amount of calculation and improving the search efficiency, we employ the method of PIO based on RHC to obtain the decision-making orders. The simulation results have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Adaptive Strategy for Commercial Aircraft with OFC Fault
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: If a fault occurs in flight control system of commercial aircraft, it will lead to a catastrophic consequence. So, it is necessary to establish an effective fault tolerant control(FTC). In this paper, an adaptive FTC was proposed. First, we built a fault aircraft model with actuator faults and introduced the Oscillatory Failure Case(OFC) fault. Then an adaptive FTC was designed which applied the method of model reference adaptive control. Finally, we established a commercial aircraft model of B747 and verified the performance of the adaptive strategy through simulation.

articleTitle: A Clock Synchronization Method for Distributed Systems Based on Fractional Calculus
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Clock Synchronization plays an important role in distributed systems. However, the practical synchronization accuracy is far below the theoretical value due to various factors. The main factor is the oscillator frequency drift causing time error between the master clock and the slave clock. Once the time error is detected and compensated, the synchronization accuracy will be greatly improved. This paper proposes a new clock synchronization method based on fractional calculus to extract out the time error in a high precision. Both simulative and experimental results have demonstrated that the proposed approach is effective.

articleTitle: A Two-Step Strategy to Fuse Height Measurements for Low-Cost Quadrotors
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For low-cost unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), it is practically important to estimate flight height using the measurements from low-cost accelerometer and barometer sensors. In this paper, we propose a simple two-step strategy to fuse the measurements from the two sensors. In the first step, two different filters, moving average filter and Kalman filter, are adopted to preprocess the measurements from accelerometer and barometer, respectively. In the second step, a properly-designed complementary filter is employed for high-precision height estimation. A large number of experimental comparison results on a small-size quadrotor demonstrate the effectiveness of the strategy.

articleTitle: Sensor Fault Diagnosis and Estimation Based on Multiple-Model Approach for Aeroengine
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, based on the multiple-model (MM) approach, a sensor fault diagnosis strategy is proposed for aero engines. The aeroengine corresponding Kalman filter bank was designed. The hypothesis test algorithm is used to find the probability of each mode, and then the sensor fault is detected and isolated based on the criterion of maximum probability. In addition, for multi-sensor fault diagnosis and estimation, a hierarchical architecture approach is used to achieve, thereby reducing the number of models and increasing the speed of calculation. In the simulation environment, the proposed multi-model method was used to study the fault diagnosis and estimation of a certain turbofan engine sensor. Simulation results show that the proposed multi-model method can effectively achieve sensor fault diagnosis and has good robustness.

articleTitle: An improved plurality average voting Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of incomplete consideration of voting conditions and redundancy of voting process and the excessive time consumption in the design of voting algorithm for multi-Modular redundant system, this paper proposes a method that arranges the difference between the sorted redundant modules into an upper triangular matrix and uses the upper triangular matrix to analyze the voting conditions. The upper triangular matrix covers all the information of the multi-Modular redundant system, and the points on the counter-diagonal of the upper triangular matrix have the maximum range of influence and the smallest deviation from the average calculation. Based on this, an improved plurality average voting algorithm (IPAV) is designed. For an N-Modular Redundant (NMR) system, the algorithm searches along the counter-diagonal of the upper triangular matrix and chooses the set, in which the maximum number of redundant modules satisfies n/2, to perform an averaging vote. A test method that can measure the execution time and the reliability of the algorithm is designed and tested in a Quadruple Modular Redundant system. Compared with the plurality median voter (PMV) and the adaptive majority voter (AMV), the empirical results show that IPAV has the obvious advantages of lowest time consumption and high reliability.

articleTitle: An Improved UAV Coverage Search Route Planning Method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The coverage search route planning method of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) plays an important role in improving the ability of reconnaissance and surveillance, information acquisition and endurance. When the search area is a convex polygon, the usage of the traditional algorithm can help to calculate the width of search area rapidly and accurately, and find the corresponding support parallel line direction. If UAV flies straight along the support parallel line direction, the number of turns will be the least, so the path of coverage search can be the shortest. However, the relationship between minimum turning radius and the width of sensor detection area is not considered in traditional planning algorithm. When the minimum turning radius of UAV become larger, there will be gaps between the routes, then it can't completely cover the detection area. In order to solve the problem, a U-turn method is proposed in this paper, and the traditional planning algorithm has been improved. Finally, the effectiveness of the improved algorithm is verified by the simulation experiment.

articleTitle: Task-oriented Combat Decision Making Methods of Unmanned Surface Vehicle Swarm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Unmanned Surface Vehicle swarm combat will be the main tactical mode in the future. Based on the requirements of multi-USV executing combat missions, agent-based USV swarm combat overall framework is designed and analyzed in details. Then we investigate USV offensive and defensive strategies for executing different mission tasks. With the designed USV swarm decision-making rules, each individual USV can perform strategies such as following, avoiding, striking and cooperating. The feasibility and effectiveness of USV swarm combat decision making methods was verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Pseudo-spectral-enhanced Output Regulation for Hypersonic Flight Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: An asymptotic flight tracking controller is constructed by output regulation technology for hypersonic flight vehicles subjected to nonlinear non-minimum phase dynamic. The standard dynamic inversion technology cannot be utilized directly in control system design due to the unstable zero-dynamics in hypersonic flight vehicle. Hence, the output regulation theory is investigated to design a nonlinear asymptotic tracking controller in sinusoidal flight maneuver cases. Meanwhile, pseudo spectral technology is introduced to solve the center manifold equation in the standard output regulation problem. Finally, Numerical Simulation shows that the proposed control scheme can afford favorable tracking performance and suppress unstable zero dynamics effectively.

articleTitle: A Preliminary Study on Civil Aircraft Post-flight Automatic Maintenance Test Philosophy and Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Civil aircraft maintenance tests are used to detect latent failures in the Flight Control System (FCS) that cannot be detected through continuous monitoring. And each maintenance tests have their required exposure time intervals. The exposure time intervals are used to determine whether the maintenance tests will be executed automatically or manually. This Paper focused on the study of automated tests hosted in the FCS, which do not require the maintenance user intervention, and these tests will be automatically initiated following rollout phase. Automated tests are capable of commanding the primary surfaces and injecting failures into the FCS components, therefore they will be allowed to execute only when the aircraft is in a safe state. The suite of logic that manages and controls automated tests could contribute to hazardous or catastrophic hazards. This logic is referred as post flight and needs to be investigated to ensure the safety of the civil aircraft.

articleTitle: Fault detection and isolation for GNSS/SINS integrated navigation system based on MSS and PNN
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper present a fault detection and isolation method for GNSS/SINS integrated navigation system based on MSS (Multiple Solution Separation) and PNN (Probability Neural Network). The method can also be well applied in the field of general aviation aircraft. Firstly the GNSS/SINS tightly integrated navigation system is designed. Based on the model, the principles and methods of MSS used for fault detection are deduced. Then the fault isolation method using PNN are analyzed too. Lastly, by establishing a simulation system, the analysis and availability for the method are verified.

articleTitle: Flocking Control of Multi-Quadrotor System of Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper studies the flocking problem for Quadrotors in three-dimensional space. Each Quadrotor's attitude dynamics is considered. Motivated by consensus algorithms of multi-agent and attitude control of aircraft, we design a distributed control law to achieve the flocking of quadrotors. The convergence is proved by Lyapunov function and Lie group algebra. And the simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed control law.

articleTitle: A New Method for Estimating the Measurement Noise Covariance Matrix of Filtering Algorithms in Geomagnetic Navigation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In the research of geomagnetic navigation, it is difficult to accurately estimate the measurement noise covariance matrix (R) of filtering algorithms, due to the existence of the geomagnetic field model error. In this paper, the method based on the geomagnetic field model error for estimating R is proposed for the first time. The magnetometer measurement error is much smaller than the geomagnetic field model error, which can be approximately estimated by using the real-flight data of the Swarm Alpha. Consequently, the measurement noise of the system is mainly determined by the geomagnetic field model error, rather than the magnetometer measurement error, and R can be therefore obtained by reference to the geomagnetic field model error. Simulations with the real-flight data of the Swarm Alpha have been performed and the results show the validity of the proposed method, which can estimate the parameter R in extended Kalman filter (EKF) and unscented Kalman filter (UKF).

articleTitle: Predictive Guidance Scheme with NAR Neural Network for Autonomous Aerial Refueling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In order to improve the passive tracking situation of receiver aircraft for drogue during the docking phase of AAR (autonomous aerial refueling), a strategy of AAR predictive guidance scheme based on NAR (Nonlinear Auto Regressive) neural network model is proposed. The NAR neural network model is used to predict the future position of the drogue as the target point of receiver aircraft. The simulation is carried out by Monte Carlo target test. The simulation results indicate that the proposed algorithm possesses high prediction precision and significantly enhances the success rate of AAR, which is of crucial importance in achievement of AAR technique.

articleTitle: Multi-UAV Cooperative Navigation Algorithm Based on Federated Filtering Structure
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Navigation error of each UAV with low-precision navigation devices in UAV formation will increase rapidly over time, and centralized Kalman filtering in cooperative navigation will lead to a sharp increase in the amount of calculations for a single machine. A UAV cooperative navigation algorithm based on federated filtering structure is proposed aiming at these problems. Firstly, the state model of each sub-filter is established, and the measurement model of the sub-filter is constructed based on the output information and the relative navigation information of the navigation system. Secondly, the main filter measurement equation is constructed by the joint error correction of the UAV navigation systems. The federal filtering structure is used to estimate the error of each UAV navigation system and the Kalman filter is improved. Simulation results show that this algorithm can effectively slow down the divergence of navigation errors in each UAVs and compared with the centralized filter reduce the computation of leader.

articleTitle: Determination of The Barrier in The Qualitatively Pursuit-evasion Differential Game
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: A new game scenario, the process of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and unmanned ground vehicle(UGV) pursuit-evasion games affected by obstacles, is present in this paper. Using the differential game theory pursuit-evasion game is analyzed, and the determination process of the avoidance zone and the catchment boundary is given in the presence of obstacles in the game environment. Based on their respective movement characteristics, the dynamics equations of the two parts are established. The game strategy is got through the analyze of dynamics characteristics. Discussing the termination of game, the barrier were got with the impact of obstacles. The simulations with analyze was given.

articleTitle: Effect Analysis of Missile Decoy Distribution on Exo-atmosphere Kinetic Interceptor
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the missile defense technology, the diversification confrontation measures of missile are widely used. The confrontation process between interceptor and missile equipped with Decoy is analyzed. The relative model between interceptor and missile is established in rotation coordinate of Line of Sight. The interceptor’s endgame effect is studied based on CADET (Covariance Analysis Describing Function Technique). Finally, the effectiveness is taken to demonstrate though a numerical simulation in this paper.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Based Framework for Textual Requirement Analysis and Model Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Requirement analysis is a key part of systems engineering process. Analyzing requirements correctly and creating design model sequentially could be critical to the whole process of a product development. Nevertheless, requirement text handling and model transferring could be really time-consuming and error-prone. Thus, we proposed an artificial intelligence based framework to deal with textual requirement handling and model creation. With deep learning and natural language process skills, our approach could be able to analyze textual requirements automatically, and then create the related models. This would indeed alleviate the work of engineers and promote the efficiency and quality of product development process. With our limited knowledge, our paper is the first one to propose the deep learning and NLP based framework to automatically create requirement models.

articleTitle: UAVs’ autonomous collision avoidance in urban space
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Small UAVs are seeking wide usage in urban space for its advantageous performance. However, there are crowded with static and dynamic buildings, causing serious challenges for UAVs’ safety. This paper proposes a novel autonomous collision avoidance method based on time-obstacle dynamic map. First, the state estimation and trajectory prediction are performed based on extended Kalman filtering. Second, the time-obstacle dynamic map is constructed via introducing time axis. Third, the flyable paths are searched on the basis of breadth first approach and then the optimal path can be obtained through A-Star algorithm. Finally, the simulation results have shown that the proposed collision avoidance method can avoid immobile building and moving obstacles, and making a safe path for UAVs in urban space

articleTitle: Composite Finite-time Guidance Law for Homing Missile
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, the terminal guidance problem of a missile intercepting maneuvering target is studied. The main contributions are threefold. Firstly, a composite finite-time guidance law based on finite-time stability theory and nonlinear disturbance observer (NDOB) technique is proposed, which can effectively handle guidance system such that the missile intercepts a maneuvering target with zero miss distance. Secondly, with the help of NDOB, the switching gain of the composite guidance law only need to be chosen larger than the bounds of the target acceleration estimation error, which are usually much smaller than those of target acceleration. As a result, it is efficient to reduce the chattering phenomenon while the disturbance rejection performance of guidance system can well be maintained. The last but not least, a general class of finite-time guidance laws is proposed. The design method will become much more flexible and convenient. Finally, simulation results on missile-target interception example are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Robust Stabilization Control for Attitude Angular Speeds of Strong-Coupling Aircraft Based on a Class of ESO
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Aiming at the characteristics with respect to strong couplings, complicated nonlinearities and high uncertainties existing in the three-channel movement of aircraft, a three degree-of-freedom (3-DOF) robust stabilization control approach is proposed for the attitude angular speeds of aircraft. Based on the coupled equations of aircraft attitude dynamics, a nonlinear design model is presented facing to the 3-DOF stabilization control on attitude angular speeds. In order to solve the robustness deficiencies of traditional dynamic inversion control (DIC), one multi-variable linear extended state observer (MVLESO) is introduced to constitute a MVLESO-based robust DIC scheme. Furthermore, this control scheme is applied to realize the asymptotic stabilization on the attitude angular speeds of aircraft. From the computer simulation on a strong-coupling aircraft plant, the proposed stabilization control scheme can guarantee the attitude angular speeds converge to the equilibrium states fast, and the robust property against model uncertainties and structural disturbances can also be improved.

articleTitle: UCAV formation collaborative trajectory planning based on hp adaptive pseudospectral method
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The collaborative trajectory planning of UCAV formation is a complex nonlinear optimization problem. At first, according to the analysis of the UCAV formation attack process, the synergy elements are given. Then according to combining the UCAV kinematics/dynamics model and the relative motion equation, the UCAV formation trajectory planning is established. And the threat of single UCAV, the threat of formation members, the time cost value, and the time error of the execution instruction are considered. Finally, in order to solve the problem, hp adaptive pseudospectral method is proposed. The simulation results for the UCAV formation trajectory planning show that the proposed method is feasible.

articleTitle: Sensor Composite Faults Estimation and Control for Hypersonic Flight Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This study presents a sensor composite faults estimation and fault-tolerant control (FTC) for a nonlinear Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy model of hypersonic flight vehicle (HFV). A novel generalized fuzzy observer is designed to estimate sensor cascading faults integrating constant offset and time-varying gain faults. Then, a fault accommodation is addressed to compensate the faults through estimation results. The sufficient condition for the existence of the fuzzy observer and controller is derived based on Lyapunov theory. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed fault estimation and FTC scheme.

articleTitle: Real-time Obstacle Map Reconstruction by Sensors with Limited Field of View for Vision Based Autonomous Robot
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Sensors on mobile robot usually have limited field of view which is unfavorable for obstacle detection. To make indoor mobile robot avoid obstacle automatically using these sensors, this paper presents a method to reconstruct obstacle map originated in human behavior. It gives every observed obstacle a credibility and if it is not observed, the credibility will decrease in time until 0. By this way, the different observed obstacles information with time can be integrated into one obstacle map. It does not use feature mapping and only does some matrix operations on the obstacle information so it has high reliability. The experiment shows the algorithm has good performance and can fit in variable environment.

articleTitle: Robust Output-Feedback Control by Simultaneous Estimation of System State and Disturbance Input
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper investigates a robust output-feedback control scheme for a class of vehicle systems, which is obtained by combining uncertainty and disturbance estimator (UDE) and Lunberger state observer (LSO) techniques. Two important features of the scheme are: (1) a compensation signal generated by a properly designed UDE is included in both the LSO and controller to reject input disturbances; (2) a new parameter mapping is introduced for parameter tuning to obtain small steady-state errors. The parameter conditions that ensure the closed-loop system is input-to-state stable is identified. We find from the condition that: owing to the coupling between the LSO and UDE, the parameter set for the LSO with disturbance compensation is larger than that for the LSO without disturbance compensation. Both numerical simulation and experimental results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the scheme and the main finding of the paper.

articleTitle: Finite-Thrust Trajectory Optimal of Earth Orbit Transfer with J2 Perturbation Considered by Homotopic Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Finite-thrust earth orbit transfer is studied with J2 perturbation considered in the dynamics. Firstly, the state equation of system is set up. Then based on minimum principle, the minimum conditions are readjusted. The whole solve process is then proposed. To reduce the difficulty in guessing of initial state values, method of extending the J2 step by step is introduced. Simulation result proved that the algorithm is practical and effective, which can be well applied in earth orbit transfers.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influential Factors of Inertial Navigation Platform Powering on Continuously
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The new requirement for inertial navigation platforms is continuous long-term power work. Based on the platform structure and the error model, this paper analyzes the change of the integrated physical field caused by the continuous energization and shows that the temperature is the main factor limiting the energization time. Through the experimental analysis, we have clarified the relationship between temperature and time, and the influence of temperature on the error coefficient. It lays a foundation for further research on the control scheme of prolonging the power supply time of the platform.

articleTitle: A Guidance Method for Small Solid-Rocket Launch Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper presents a guidance method for solid-rocket launch vehicles. A three-stage launch vehicle, as illustration, the guidance algorithm is designed for the second stage and the third stage. For the second stage, the guidance algorithm guides the vehicle to a transfer orbit, and high precision orbit injection is implemented by the guidance algorithm for the third stage. Numerical simulation results show that the proposed guidance method can achieve an adequate precision with the burnout shutdown.

articleTitle: High Earth Orbital Satellite Autonomous Navigation based on Ground beacon, Ultraviolet Sensor and GNSS measurement
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: When ultraviolet sensor and GNSS navigation are applied to high earth orbital satellite navigation, the navigation accuracy is limited due to low accuracy of geocentric measurement, fewer GNSS navigation signals and poor navigation satellite geometry distribution. In this paper, high accuracy direction vector measurement of ground beacons with high accuracy is introduced for integrated navigation combing ultraviolet sensor and GNSS measurement. In order to improve the accuracy of the typical asynchronous data fusion algorithm such as sub-optimal filtering, the data fusion method based on measurement driving is studied, and a filter with variable filtering period is designed based on the extended Kalman filter algorithm. Mathematical simulation shows that the introduction of ground beacon direction vector measurement can improve the navigation accuracy from 100m to 60m when the number of visible GNSS navigation satellites is less than 4. Compared with typical asynchronous data fusion algorithms, the algorithm proposed in this paper increases navigation accuracy by 9%.

articleTitle: Design of Aircraft Control System Based on Adaptive Optimal Control
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For the uncertainty of the aircraft dynamics parameters, the adaptive control method was used to design the control parameters so as to ensure the stability of the aircraft control system. When designing the reference model of the controller, the linear quadratic optimal control method was used to make the reference model behave as a typical second-order link. Based on the Lyapunov stability theory, the self-adaptation law was deduced to ensured the closed-loop stability of the system. The simulation results showed that the control method designed in this paper can keep track of the reference model when the aircraft dynamics parameters changed.

articleTitle: Grey Prediction PID Control for Single Moving-mass Controlled Reentry Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For a single moving-mass controlled reentry vehicle, the aim of control is tracking and stabilization in roll and yaw channel, respectively. Firstly, the model of reentry vehicle is established with Coriolis Theory, and nonlinear model for design is derived. Then, grey prediction based on GM(1,1) is presented to predict the error between the rolling angle and command. And grey prediction PID controller is designed with function based on grey prediction. At last, simulation and comparison are carried out; the results show the system has better response, better adaptability and stronger robustness than traditional PID controller.

articleTitle: Research on Drogue Detection Algorithm for Aerial Refueling (IEEE/CSAA GNCC)
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV) has become more and more widely used in military and non-military applications, but endurance has become a major limiting factor in the development of UAV. In order to increase the UAV's endurance, this paper uses a vision guidance method to achieve automatic aerial refueling technology. This paper proposes an automatic refueling technology based on a deep-learning algorithm for detection. The Faster RCNN algorithm can simultaneously recognize the fuel receiver and the Drogue at long-distance and returns the center coordinate value of the receiver. If the pixel area of the identified Drogue is greater than a certain threshold, the central coordinate value of the Drogue is returned. The experiment results show that the average accuracy of the algorithm reaches 67.75%, and the real-time performance is about 5HZ.

articleTitle: Application of Distributed Data Processing System in Aerospace Industry
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The performance of domestic processors and databases cannot meet the requirements of real-time data processing and high-speed data query in aerospace industry. In order to make up for the lack of domestic hardware and software, according to the data characteristics of spacecraft, clustered servers are used to build distributed systems. New load balancing algorithms are proposed, and data mining software algorithms are designed at the Server Array level to realize the application of distributed data processing system in aerospace industry.

articleTitle: An Efficient Angular Rate Coning Algorithm for SINS
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Strapdown inertial navigation system (SINS) is widely used in aerospace field. Complex motion, such as maneuver, will lead to additional errors in the SINS attitude algorithm. Accordingly an improved coning correction form is proposed to design efficient coning algorithms for SINS with rate gyro. This new correction form contains only one vector cross product, and is constructed by changing the traditional uncompressed angular rate-based form with a given definite relationship. The given relationship is derived, and is used for designing the improved coning algorithm. By analysis and simulation, it shows that the improved coning algorithm compared with the uncompressed rate-based coning algorithm has an equivalent maneuver accuracy which is significantly higher than that of the compressed rate-based algorithm, and a much lower algorithm computation load.

articleTitle: Generalized Polynomial Chaos Based Uncertainty Propagation for Perturbed Two-body Orbits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper presents a generalized polynomial chaos based computational methodology for the uncertainty propagation problem of the perturbed two-body orbits. The key idea is to approximate the solutions of the stochastic differential equation describing the perturbed orbits with linear expansions of a series of orthogonal polynomial bases. The main uncertainty sources in the dynamical equations were firstly analyzed, and then the non-intrusive generalized polynomial chaos technique was introduced to propagate the uncertainties for the consideration of estimation accuracy and computational efficiency. Numerical simulation results validate that the proposed algorithm is effective for non-Gaussian uncertainty analysis of nonlinear systems over a long duration, providing references for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Degree of Controllability based on Gramian for Solar Sails in Artificial Lagrangian Orbits
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The model of the solar sail in the Sun-Earth system is established, the concept of degree of controllability based on controllability Gramian is introduced as well. The degree of controllability of solar sail at five artificial Lagrangian points near the sun-earth L<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> point, and the degree of controllability of solar sail at one chosen artificial Lagrangian point under different cases of control inputs are evaluated. The results reveal that the controllability of the solar sail is various due to the different locations and the distinct control inputs. The results could give us more quantitative information about the controllability of solar sail, rather than it is simply controllable or not, which may provide more effective suggestions for the design of the solar sail in the future space missions.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of Catapult Take-off for Carrier-Based Aircraft Considering the Carrier Motion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper is the simulation study of aircraft carrier catapult take-off considering various environmental factors. A general carrier-based aircraft longitudinal dynamic model based on the aerodynamic and kinematic characteristics of the different phases was established. The proposed control scheme for the climbing phase is to keep the aircraft rise steadily. Then a simulation program was conducted to identify the rationality of the model. The aircraft's state parameters of catapult take-off after leaving the ship was analyzed. Simulation results show that the model and the control scheme have a beneficial effect.

articleTitle: Taxiing Control of Full-wing Solar-powered UAV by Using Differential Propeller Thrust
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: To solve the taxiing control problem under lack of nose wheel steering system and rudder, a control approach which uses differential propeller thrust to control taxiing is proposed, with full-wing solar-powered UAV (FSUAV) as the research model. This study gives the taxiing mathematical model of FSUAV and designs a taxiing controller based on linear active disturbance rejection control method (LADRC). Simulations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the designed controller and compare with PID controller.

articleTitle: Ensemble Consider Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For the nonlinear systems, the ensemble Kalman filter can avoid using the Jacobian matrices and reduce the computational complexity. However, the state estimates still suffer greatly negative effects from uncertain parameters of the dynamic and measurement models. To mitigate the negative effects, an ensemble consider Kalman filter (EnCKF) is designed by using the “consider” approach and resampling the ensemble members in each step to incorporate the statistics of the uncertain parameters into the state estimation formulations. The effectiveness of the proposed EnCKF is verified by two numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Efficient Plane Extraction Based on Hierarchical Clustering
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Plane extraction is a crucial task for many applications such as robot navigation, SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping) and so on. Although there exists several of plane segmentation methods based on RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus), Hough transform, region growing etc. Some of these methods may not guarantee speed performance for computer vision tasks with real-time requirements. In order to improve the efficiency of the plane extraction algorithm, we propose a method based on agglomerative hierarchical clustering in this paper. Our method extracts planar surfaces in organized point clouds obtained from RGB-D sensors such as Microsoft Kinect in real time. We first divide point clouds into several groups of points as nodes. Those nodes represent point sets while the edges of the nodes represent neighborhoods. Next, we find nodes with the smallest plane fitting MSE (mean squared error) as initial nodes, and then perform agglomerative hierarchical clustering to merge nodes that belong to the same plane. We stop the step once the MSE is larger than the given threshold. Weoptimize the boundary of the extracted planes at last. We evaluate our method using the public TUM and SegComp datasets. Experiments show that the proposed approach can detect planar surfaces efficiently and correctly compared with other state-of-art methods.

articleTitle: Sigmiod based anti-disturbances trajectory tracking for quadrotor UAV under gyroscope noise
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, a Sigmiod based anti-disturbances trajectory tracking controller is developed to cope with the trajectory tracking problem of the quadrotor under external disturbances, model uncertainties and gyroscope noise. Firstly, the accurate nonlinear dynamic model of quadrotor UAV is established. Then, based on the hierarchical control principle, the trajectory tracking controller is designed as position loop and attitude loop respectively, each loop constructs the corresponding controller by feedback linearization. In addition, the high-order sigmoid tracking differentiator (STD) is developed to generate the required differential signal and arrange expected transition process, synchronously, the sigmoid disturbance observer (SDO) with the same frame as the STD is applied to reconstruct the lump disturbances of the attitude loop and the position loop. At last, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed controller not only ensures small tracking error and strong noise suppression, but also simplifies the structure of controller and make it easy to adjust controller parameters.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Performance Test Method for GNSS Receiver Based on Vehicular Microwave Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The dynamic performance test and evaluation of high precision GNSS receiver was a major technical problem in the field of navigation and surveying. The major difficulty was to obtain higher accuracy reference data, and to remain the stability of relative position between the reference equipment (RE) and the equipment under test (EUT) in dynamic conditions. In this paper, a dynamic verification method based on vehicular microwave anechoic chamber (VMAC) was proposed. Far field conditions was fulfilled in a vehicular chamber, in which a transponder was used to transmit GNSS signal into the chamber, to make sure EUT and RE receive identical signals. Thus, the measurements of EUT and RE were equivalent to the phase center of the transponder antenna. The test of the VMAC method was presented and its implementation was introduced. Test results show that the VMAC method can be used for dynamic pseudo-range positioning accuracy test, and carrier-phase differential positioning accuracy evaluation. Besides, this method can also be applied for equipment development and design, technical identification, production testing, periodic verification etc.

articleTitle: Pseudospectral-based Multiple Missiles Salvo Attack with Angle Constrains
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this thesis, the guidance problem of multiple missiles attack a single target simultaneously is converted to the optimal control problem, which can be solved by the hp-adaptive pseudospectral method. The time-varying proportional navigation (PN) gain is designed to satisfy the required tactical and impact-time constraints. Numerical simulation of the engagement situation demonstrates the performance and feasibility of this simultaneously attack method.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerant Control for the Quadrotor Attitude Using a SOS Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper addresses the nonlinear H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> fault tolerant control (FTC) problem for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), with convex polytopic faults in motors. Based on Rodrigues parameter description, the attitude dynamic of the quadrotor is modeled in a state dependent linear-like form. By using Lyapunov stability and positive polynomial theories, the sufficient conditions for stabilization with and without H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> performance of the UAV system are formulated in terms of state-dependent linear matrix inequalities which can be verified by sostools in MATLAB. Numerical simulation results show the effectiveness in accommodating loss of motor effectiveness.

articleTitle: Webpages Classification Based on Deep Belief Network Using Images and Text Information
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, Deep Belief Network(DBN) is used for drug-related webpages classification. HTML parsing is used to extract image-label text and body text, FOCARSS method is used to choose effective images. text representation is generated by BOW model, images representation is generated by BOF model. We concatenate images and text representation to generate final representation. It is shown that DBN's classification accuracy is higher than BPNN's classification accuracy, and better than that of single-modal information.

articleTitle: Fault Detection for Redundant SIMU on SVD Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Based on the singular value decomposition (SVD) algorithm, this paper proposes the singular value decomposition optimization algorithm for redundant strapdown inertial measurement unit (SIMU) fault detection. Based on the existing singular value decomposition algorithm, the columns of decoupling matrix are unitized. In addition, the decision function for isolation is corrected. Finally, the fault detection of the redundant SIMU regular dodecahedron configuration is simulated. By comparing the simulation results of the SVD algorithm and the SVD optimization algorithm, it proves that the SVD optimization algorithm is the feasible and effective.

articleTitle: A Novel Wind-field Reconstruction Approach for Quadrotors Using Inertial Measurement Units
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: A novel wind field calibration and reconstruction method applied to quadrotor is proposed in this paper through the utilization of inertial measurement units. The realationship between the attitude of the quadrotor and the wind field information is utilized to obtain wind speed and direction. Compared with the traditional method, only inertial sensors are required in our approach rather than extra sensors to estimate the wind filed. Wind information obtained by the experimental flight data of quadrotor highly coincided with the results from the automatic weather station, which manifested the effectiveness and accruacy of our method.

articleTitle: Design of Load Balancing Strategy of UAV Flight Control Software
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For the UAV flight control software with complicated function and high real-time requirements, the static load sharing strategy and dynamic load balancing algorithm is designed by utilizing software bus which uses the flight control computer with distributed architecture based on CAN bus as a platform. In addition, the mechanism of function module migration is designed. These methods solved the declining operating efficiency and waste of resources which is caused by the load imbalance of nodes in the distributed flight control system and keeps the system performing efficiently and continuously. Finally, the result of experiments show that two types of load-sharing algorithm all can schedule the functional modules accurately and guarantee the real-time performance, also improved the reliability and security of the distributed flight control system.

articleTitle: Relative Lambert Problem of Near Coplanar Long-Range Relative Motion
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The relative Lambert problem based on a near-coplanar long-range relative motion in circular reference orbit is investigated. The relative Lambert problem consists of determining the relative velocity given relative positions at two known times. As for the short distance relative Lambert problem, an analytic solution is obtained by using matrix inversion based on the Clohessy-Wiltshire equation. Then a second-order relative motion Lambert solver is derived from the second-order Clohessy-Wiltshire equation. However, the admissible relative distance between spacecrafts is still far smaller than the semi-major axis of the chief spacecraft. This paper aims to enlarge the admissible relative distance. To solve the corresponding relative Lambert problem, a time-explicit analytic description of a near-coplanar long-range relative motion in circular reference orbit is introduced to provide a two-pulse relative transfer strategy. It is worth pointing out that the angle between the inertial position vector of the chief and the inertial position vector of the deputy can be any value, which means the admissible relative distance can be very large. The choice of the transfer time is also important. As a result of the existence of singular points, the transfer time should be far away from these singular points. In addition, the transfer time should ensure that the initial impulse meets the corresponding condition of the analytical solution to the long range relative motion. Four numerical results show that the proposed method to solve the relative Lambert problem is indeed effective and feasible.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Ground Target Tracking for Fixed-wing UAV
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In the fixed-wing UAV ground target tracking problem, the UAV is equipped with photoelectric sensor which can rotate for positioning the ground target. Geometric relationship between the UAV and target described by the direction of sensor is analyzed, which is used to guide the UAV tracking ground target, and it also used to establish the simulation model. The guidance strategy is established and a lead compensation method is proposed. Finally, a dynamic simulation model of the UAV and the flight control system is established to verify the strategy.

articleTitle: Capturability Analysis of Pure Proportional Navigation Guidance Law for Intercepting Hypersonic Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper describes the capturability analysis concerning pure proportional navigation (PPN) guidance law for hypersonic interception. Using a modified polar coordinate, the expression of the three-dimensional (3D) relative kinematic model of the missile and target becomes simpler. Then, the capture conditions of PPN guidance law, which are sufficient and necessary conditions for hypersonic interception, are derived by using an auxiliary function. Finally, the simulation results indicate that smaller navigation constant and bigger speed ratio render a smaller capture region for intercepting high speed targets.

articleTitle: The Application of Soft-sensing Based on LS_SVM within Free Search
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of parameter optimization in soft sensor model based on least squares support vector machine, we used free search algorithm to optimize it, so as to improve the accuracy of soft measurement. Taking the soft measurement of gas content in gas - liquid two phase flow as an example, in this paper, four intelligent optimize arithmetic free search, PSO, GA and grid-search) were compared based on optimize precision. The experiment proves that, LS_SVM model based on free search gives better estimate precision and better generalization capabilities than the other three optimization methods. It provides a better prediction method for soft sensing.

articleTitle: Determination of take-off constraints for the aerospace vehicle
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper studies the conditions of the successful takeoff and climbing of the aerospace vehicle. By analyzing the longitudinal kinematics model and dynamic model of the vehicle, the take-off constraints determined by integrating with the lift-drag ratio, thrust-to-weight ratio, flight speed and take-off weight. Moreover, the algebraic form of the maximum take-off weight is also derived to ensure that the aircraft can successfully take off under a fixed configuration. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Decentralized Fixed-Time Attitude Synchronization Control for Spacecraft Formation Flying
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, the decentralized fixed-time attitude synchronization problem is considered for multiple rigid spacecraft system. A multispacecraft fixed-time-based terminal sliding mode is designed, which possesses the predefined convergence time independent of initial condition. Then, the decentralized attitude control laws by employing the fixed-time-based terminal sliding mode are proposed, which can avoid the singularity and guarantee the attitude tracking errors converge to zero in fixed time. Finally, numerical simulations are presented to demonstrate the performance of the new controllers.

articleTitle: The Impact angle guidance law Parameter design strategy Consider final speed constraint
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This note studies the problem of impact falling angle guidance by considering the terminal speed constraint and proposes a new guidance parameter design strategy based on the law of falling angle guidance that adapts to the terminal speed is proposed. To this end, firstly, the general form of the extended trajectory shaping guidance law was deduced, and the non-dimensional acceleration characteristics of the guidance law were analyzed. Then, based on this, the influence of the change of the guidance law parameters on the dimensionless maneuvering energy is studied. A strategy for adjusting the guidance law parameters based on the end flight speed prediction results is proposed to satisfy the end speed constraints. Finally, the effectiveness of this strategy is verified by nonlinear ballistic simulation.

Author Keywords: the law of trajectory shaping guidance

articleTitle: Online Identification of Stability Margin Based on Frequency Response Estimation
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In order to improve the control performance of the aircraft and achieve on-line control, it is necessary to obtain the stability margin of the system in real time and design online attitude controller. In this paper, the stability margin online identification method is studied. Based on the Chirp-Z transform and frequency response estimation method, excitation signals are added to obtain the system's stability margin online. Simulation results show that the method proposed has high recognition accuracy and can be applied to real aircraft and used in online controller design.

articleTitle: Robust Model Predictive Fault-Tolerant Control for Time-delay Uncertain Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: For a class of time-delay discrete systems with constraints, actuator faults and polytopic-type uncertainties, the problem of robust fault-tolerant control is studied in this paper. Firstly, a new state space model with output error is introduced for reference trajectory tracking control, which provides more scope for controller designs and improves control effect. Then based on the predictive control theorem, a min-max robust model predictive control (RMPC) algorithm is proposed, which considers time delay and the fault model. Using linear matrix inequality (LMI) technology, the min-max optimization problem is transformed into a minimization problem. Finally, the asymptotic stability of close-looped system is proved and the algorithm comparison experimental results on the quadrotor semi-physical simulation platform validate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: On SLAM Based on Monocular Vision and Lidar Fusion System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: This paper presents a method of fusion of lidar and camera multisensor data fusion systems, which compensates the shortcomings of monocular camera-based navigation system and Lidar-based navigation system. Because of the different imaging principle of lidar and camera, unify two coordinate systems before being calibrated. In order to complete the fusion and compensation between the lidar and camera in the data layer, the Rodriguez matrix is used to register the measured parameters. Then, the high accuracy and registered parameters are obtained by improved Danish iteration method with variable weights based on collinearity equation. Texture seams in color images are also differential corrected to provide the depth image of a high-resolution scene, which containing depth information of the unmanned vehicle. The new Slam algorithm is also designed by Invoking the Find-Contour function and Contour-Area function in Open CV library. In addition, the experiments prove the better performance of new SLAM method.

articleTitle: Regress Analysis Filtering Algorithm for Measuring Time Delay Systems
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, high precision filtering problem is addressed for linear and nonlinear systems with fixedly delayed measurements. Based on the regression analysis theory, the measurement equation is reconstructed and the regression analysis filtering algorithm for measuring time-delay systems is proposed. Simulation results show that, compared with conventional measuring time delay filtering algorithms, new algorithm has higher estimation accuracy. This method is the theoretical foundation for the further application of statistical theory in the field of control.

articleTitle: Microfabrication and Measurement of Rb-Ne Microcell for Chip-Scale Atomic Clocks
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: We report the fabrication of a micro vapor cell which has Rb and Ne inside with internal volumes of several millimeters, which is the key component of chip-scale atomic devices like clocks and magnetometers. The cells were filled with Ne at a controlled pressure as the buffer gas by using glass-silicon anodic bonding techniques and dispenser pills of SAES Getters. And a special two-step bonding method was taken to avoid breakdown caused by the buffer gas and to secure the quality of the bonding. We also built an optical measuring system and measured the coherent population trapping (CPT) resonance of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">85</sup>Rb D1 line with a linewidth below 2.0 kHz and a contrast about 1.1%. Zeeman spectrum for CPT resonance was also detected in these microcells. These results show that these vapor cells are capable to be used in atomic clocks or magnetometers.

articleTitle: High Fidelity Satellite to Satellite Tracking toolkit (HFSST) for Navigation Mission Design
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The HFSST “High Fidelity Satellite to Satellite Tracking toolkit” is a tool for space navigation mission analysis design. The inputs of the toolkit are the configurations of the mission. The outputs are the ranging data between different satellites for navigation, as well as the reports on the performance of the system. The content of these reports include the physical visibilities, the relative geometry as well as the measurement noise between satellites participating in a mission. Physical visibilities are evaluated based on the geometric relationship between the satellites and the celestial bodies, as well as the power level of the ranging signals. Which concern the attitude pointing of the satellites, the mounting positions, directions and patterns of antennas, the signal travel losses as well as the threshold of the receiver. The toolkit also includes orbital model, attitude model, and signal model as well as visualization module. These make it suitable to develop elaborated analysis of satellite navigation missions whether near Earth or deep into space. Example from an actual mission that a satellite on High Elliptical Orbit (HEO) tracks side lobe signals of the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) for navigation is demonstrated to show the features and usages of the toolkit.

articleTitle: Matching Method of Accelerometer Scale Factor for Gravity Gradiometer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The output signal of the rotating accelerometer gravity gradiometer instrument (GGI) is extremely complicated in the real gravity gradient measurement environment. Many kinds of perturbations and noises are unavoidable in real GGI systems, among all the various errors, the inconsistency of scale factors has a great influence on the resolution of the rotating accelerometer gravity gradiometer. To reduce this specific error, this paper presents a new algorithm to adjust the accelerometer scale factor. First, the band-passing filter was adopted to filtrate the output of the two opposing accelerometers. Then, the signal was demodulated from the output of the band-passing filter. This processing method is the same to the output signal of the other pair of accelerometers and the total output signal of GGI. With the three demodulation results, smoothing filtering method and real time PID feedback algorithm were used to adjust the accelerometer internal torque coils to adjust the scale factor in time. Finally, by using the method proposed in this paper, the experiment results verify that the inconsistency of the scale factor of four accelerometers on GGI was dramatically improved and the precision of gradient signal is further improved.

articleTitle: Cooperative Guidance against Stationary and Non-maneuvering Targets
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: A cooperative guidance law is proposed for salvo attack of multi-missiles. The proposed guidance law focuses on the stationary target firstly, in which the leader employs the arc guidance to precisely estimate its impact time, while followers utilize the arc-straight-line guidance to attain the consensus of the impact time with the leader. Then, a prediction method for the terminal position of the target is derived to extend the cooperative guidance law to address a non-maneuvering target. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the cooperative guidance law.

articleTitle: A New Three-dimensional Tracking Guidance Based on Full State Coupling
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: A new three dimensional tracking guidance based on full state coupling for hypersonic glide phase is proposed. Firstly, the dynamics formulation of position state in local coordinate frame is derived in conjunction with longitudinal and lateral trajectory state coupling relationship. In order to fast solve the problem of trajectory generation with multiple constraints and flight task requirements, all of the trajectory states have been normalized. Secondly, on the basis of dynamics equations, a three-dimensional coupling guidance model has been built with the help of proper performance index. Finally, simulation results with common aero vehicle (CAV-H) show that the trajectory obtained by proposed approach can well perform the tracking task during entry.

articleTitle: Research on Fault-tolerant Control for SRM Air Gap Eccentricity Fault
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: In this paper, for switched reluctance motor, a fault-tolerant control for the air gap eccentricity fault based on hardware optimization and control strategy design is proposed. Firstly, in hardware optimization, based on the analysis of the influence from winding mode on air gap eccentricity fault, the suppression of imbalanced electromagnetic force under the condition of air gap eccentricity fault is achieved using current self-balancing of stator winding parallel structure. Based on the hardware optimization, a fault-tolerant controller based on current adaptive control is designed, for the objective of unbalanced electromagnetic force suppression, the current active control under fault condition is realized. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle Occasional Flameout Diagnosis Based on Logistic Regression Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Logistic regression algorithm is used to diagnose car occasional flameout. In the process of identifying the fault, the impact of each component on the fault is analyzed to improve the recognition accuracy.

articleTitle: On Region of Attraction Analysis of Nonlinear Flight Dynamic System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Current practice for flight stability analysis relies heavily on linear analysis and nonlinear, high-fidelity simulations. In the paper, the method of region of attraction analysis based on Sum Of Square (SOS) theory is proposed and applied on nonlinear system to estimate its stability. The polynomial model of aircraft is deduced from the nonlinear dynamic model, and then the stable flight region is calculated. Simulation results show that the aircraft can resume stable flight while its initial condition is in the region of attraction. The methodology provides a new way to research the stability and control of the nonlinear flight dynamic system. In addition, it has practical significance for guaranteeing the flight safety.

articleTitle: An Architecture of Mission-oriented Multi-aircraft Sensor Management System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: With the rapid development of multi-aircraft network combat, a new demand for sensor management system is raised. This paper proposes a novel architecture of task-oriented multi-aircraft sensor management system, which is based on multi-agent. According to requirements of multi-aircraft network combat, function division, module definition and mutual information of the architecture is given. A preliminary simulation is carried out to verify the feasibility of the architecture. Driven by missions, this architecture has characteristics of excellent openness and adaptability.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Isolation Based on Extreme Learning Machine optimized by Genetic Algorithm for Flight Control System
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Fault detection and isolation (FDI) plays an important role in the safe operation of flight control system. For a complex flight control system, it is difficult to build an accurate physical model, so data-driven method has emerged. In this paper, an extreme learning machine (ELM) method optimized by genetic algorithm (GA) is proposed. Compared with traditional feed-forward neural network, ELM has great generalization performance at a high learning speed. Furthermore, GA is used in this method to adjust hidden nodes parameters to find the most suitable parameters that minimizes the ELM model error. What is more, different fault models are built respectively, so as to achieve the purpose of fault isolation. All in all, the proposed method can isolate fault while optimizing the extreme learning machine.

articleTitle: On a Specific Force Based Tansfer Alignment Method of Strapdown Navigation System in Targeting Pod
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The strapdown navigation system installed in targeting pod adopts low precision inertial components and the transfer alignment process is performed in low dynamic conditions. In view of the above phenomena, a method of `specific force integral/angular velocity matching' is proposed, and the error model of the master and slave inertial navigation system is derived. The observability of the system states is analysed in condition of various instrument precisions and maneuvers. The simulation process is designed and the result shows that the misalignment of the method fits the performance index of the rapid transfer alignment.

articleTitle: On Active Sidestick Force Control Strategy Technology
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: The future aircraft control system will be based on FBW and active sidestick, which can provide various force-feeling and force-control. This paper introduces the features of active sidestick, develops an active sidestick system based on sinus-wave motor, proposes a control law based on 3-loops control to realize the precise control, a method to change characteristics by impedance control, an accumulation control strategy to solve the problem of precise return to neutral position, and lists the result of force-position curve and stick shaker, this system can realize a higher control accuracy and stability, the response ability in low frequency, which has an important significance to engineering prototype.

articleTitle: Opto-Electronic Platform Stabilized Anti-disturbance Tracking Controller Based on Reference Observer and Disturbance Observer
publicationTitle: 2018 IEEE CSAA Guidance, Navigation and Control Conference (CGNCC)
abstract: Aiming at the two axis Opto-Electronic Platform, in order to diminish the influences caused by the friction disturbance moment and the disturbance of the UAV angular motion, disturbance compensation control based on a disturbance observer is introduced into this system.
